newsitem.title: USA: IRIDIUM satellite launch delayed again.
newsitem.headline: IRIDIUM satellite launch delayed again.

text.p: IRIDIUM LLC said the launch of its first three satellites has been delayed again, this time due to a problem with a microwave link discovered during the launch countdown early Thursday.
The launch was postponed until Friday morning at 0535 PST/1335 GMT.
Motorola Inc has about a 25 percent stake in IRIDIUM, a consortium that is working to provide a global telecommunications network using 66 low-orbit satellites.
IRIDIUM said the problem Thursday involved the loss of a vital data microwave link to U.S. Air Force range instrumentation, and the Air Force is working to resolve it.
The launch was initially scheduled for Wednesday but was postponed because of a "minor technical anomaly," IRIDIUM said.
IRIDIUM is an international consortium of 17 companies and organizations, including Motorola, Sprint Corp, Lockheed Martin Corp, Pacific Electric Wire & Cable Co Ltd of Taiwan and Raytheon Co.
The three satellites are to be carried into orbit by a McDonnell Douglas Corp Delta II rocket from Vandenberg Air Force Base in Lompoc, Calif.
